patch_description: Crossover of the k-shortest-simple-paths candidate pool (which gave the best cost, 1015.93) with the congestion-aware marginal-cost assignment from the Monte-Carlo variant. For each destination we enumerate k cheap alternative simple paths (pruned to within a slack of the best), then assign partitions greedily by marginal cost: base edge cost scaled by a load-vs-throughput penalty, so partitions spread across parallel low-cost routes and avoid stacking on congested edges. This removes the expensive random sampling while retaining load balancing across networks.
